At Batchworth Community Council, we want this website to reflect the needs and wants of our community. If there is anything that you feel we may have missed here, please do let us know: email: clerk@batchworth-ecc.gov.uk or phone 01923 590201
Following a campaign and a ballot, Batchworth Community Council was granted a Re-organisation Order in 2016. The first elections for the Community Council took place in May 2017 and eight Councillors elected – four for each of the two wards which make up the Council area; Rickmansworth Town Ward and Moor Park & Eastbury Ward.

Consultation - stage two
Three Rivers District Council is undertaking a Community Governance Review (CGR) to consider whether the current parish governance arrangements across the district continue to reflect the identities and interests of local communities and provide effective and convenient local government.
Following the first stage of consultation, the council has considered the feedback received from residents, parish councils and other interested parties, alongside the proposals discussed by the Policy and Resources Committee.
We are now inviting residents, businesses and community organisations to have their say on the proposals being considered as part of the second stage of the review. These include potential changes to parish boundaries, parish ward boundaries, ward names and governance arrangements in certain areas of the district.
The consultation provides an opportunity to comment on the proposed changes, suggest alternatives and share any additional information that the council should consider.
No final decisions have been made. The responses received during this consultation will help inform the council's final recommendations and ensure that any changes appropriately reflect the needs and identities of the communities they affect.
We encourage everyone with an interest in their local community to take part and have their say.
Please review the relevant proposals and accompanying maps before completing the consultation.
What is a Community Governance Review?
A Community Governance Review (CGR) looks at how town and parish councils are set up, whether any changes are needed, and if residents would support a parish council in unparished areas.
Why are we doing the Community Governance Review?
Three Rivers District Council has received a number of requests to consider changing existing parish arrangements. Chorleywood Parish Council has requested a change to the parish wards within the parish. Croxley Green Parish Council has requested parish boundaries to be reviewed with Sarratt Parish Council. Batchworth Community Council has requested to alter the number of councillors that sit on the council and consideration of name change status.
Three Rivers District Council would also like to ask residents in Maple Cross, West Hyde, Penn and Mill End if they want a parish council for all or part of the area, whether they would prefer to join an existing neighbouring parish council, or remain unparished.
This question is being raised now because of the creation of the new, larger South West Hertfordshire Unitary Council, which will replace Three Rivers District Council in April 2028. Once the unitary council is in place, parish councils will become the closest and most local tier of government for communities.
The review also gives Three Rivers residents a chance to say what changes, if any, they would like the council to consider before the next all-out parish elections in 2027. Elections for the new unitary authorities are also due to take place in the same year.
What the review can and cannot change
The review may consider the following options:
Creating, merging, altering or abolishing parishes
The naming of parishes and the style of parishes including the potential creation of town and parish councils
The electoral arrangements for parishes. For instance, the ordinary year of elections; council size; the number of councillors to be elected to the council and parish warding
Grouping parishes under a common parish council or de-grouping parishes
Other types of local arrangements including parish meetings
The review cannot:
Change the number of councillors on Three Rivers District Council
Influence or change the amount of money that an existing parish or town council raises through Council Tax known as precept

Consultation and Engagement Charter
Our residents are at the heart of all we do. We’re committed to involving our residents in the areas where your voice can help shape our services to benefit every resident, community and business. When we’re making decisions about our county, we’ll ask for your opinions, knowledge and experience to help us get things right.
Our Charter sets out a standard for public consultation and engagement to make sure that residents have a fair say in shaping their community, driving the prosperity of our county and promoting sustainable and responsible growth.
By consultation and engagement, we mean asking our residents for their views. We’ll usually consult when we need to make a specific decision. This may be regarding a plan, policy or a service. Engagement is when we seek more general views on how we run services we provide or what should be our priorities.
Our principles of consultation and public engagement are:
We’ll consult or engage the residents and other stakeholders when the proposals affect them or when there is a reasonable expectation to consult.
We’ll use plain English and make sure our consultations are easy to understand and respond to.
We’ll provide information and support to help residents understand the subject when responding to our consultations.
We’ll make our consultations available to everyone by providing different ways to have a say, this might be through online surveys, focus groups, workshops and postal surveys.
When specific groups of people may be particularly affected by our proposals, we will set out how to identify and involve them.
We’ll make every effort to enable residents across different age and ethnic groups, backgrounds and experiences to give their views.
We’ll allow enough time for you to consider and respond to the consultations.
We’ll seek to reduce the burden of consultation by reviewing existing information such as research, surveys and public opinion polls.
All our consultations will be published on the council’s website so that residents and stakeholders can see what is up for decision and how to take part.
When the consultation ends, we will collate your responses and tell you how your views have been considered.

Statement from Angie Ridgwell, Senior Responsible Officer, Hertfordshire LGR Programme
Local Government Reorganisation is coming to Hertfordshire
This website has been designed to:
Inform and educate Hertfordshire residents on what Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is, and how it impacts them.
Provide Hertfordshire residents with the opportunity to have their say – we really want to hear from our communities.
What is LGR?
In late 2024, the Government set out plans to change how local councils across England work together. This means areas like Hertfordshire that operate a two-tier system - where some services are run by district councils and others by the county council are being asked to rethink how things are organised.
​
Faced with tough financial pressures, councils are being encouraged to find smarter ways to deliver services and make better use of public money. That’s why the Government has asked the 11 council leaders in Hertfordshire to work together and come up with a joint plan for how local government could be reshaped to better serve our communities.
​
Map of Hertfordshire districts and boroughs
We want to hear from you
This is a once in a generation change, so it is important that there is proper consideration of the options and meaningful engagement with you as residents, but also local organisations and businesses.
We want to hear your views on how we can design a system that actively supports community-led action and strong local connections.
It’s important to us that we use this once in a generation opportunity for change to shape a responsive and resilient system of local government that reflects local identity and unlocks long-term benefits for residents, businesses and communities.

W3RT CVS believes that volunteering and volunteerism are crucial to the health of our communities and as a result have worked for the past 40 years to ensure that our communities benefit from strong voluntary organisations.
Looking to Volunteer?
Volunteering is a highly rewarding way to give something back to the community, meet new people or learn a new skill and we want to make it as easy as possible for individuals or businesses to take part in volunteering opportunities. As a result, we have created a dedicated volunteering hub which lists all the volunteering opportunities in our communities.
You can access the Golden Volunteer on our W3RT Volunteering Hub webpages
here
and we hope that there are a range of opportunities that suit what you are looking for. If you have any questions or would like to know about a specific type of organisation you would like to volunteer for, you can contact the CVS team by
email
or call 07908 209908.
Looking for Volunteers?
We understand the importance of volunteers for our local charities and community groups and how they allow organisations to support their beneficiaries. Therefore, we have invested in an online volunteer recruitment platform called Golden Volunteer which will make it easier for organisations to recruit volunteers for local roles across the Watford and Three Rivers area.
You can use Golden Volunteer to promote your organisation’s volunteering opportunities, recruit and manage your volunteers and use the data collected to capture the hours given and assess the impact of the work that your volunteers are doing.
If you would like to add your volunteering opportunities onto Golden Volunteer, click
here
and to ensure that you are getting the most out of Golden Volunteer, we would encourage you to contact the CVS team to arrange an introduction session to find out more about Golden Volunteer. You can contact the CVS team by
email
or call 07908 209908.
Other Volunteering support
As well as using Golden Volunteer to help with volunteer recruitment, W3RT CVS supports voluntary organisations to ensure all aspects volunteering. For example:
Supporting you design and tailor volunteer role descriptions to ensure that potential volunteers understand the roles they are applying for.
Understanding and managing safeguarding and GDPR responsibilities for volunteers.
Developing policies and procedures to help groups manage, engage and recognise their volunteers.
Holding an annual Volunteers’ Fair to support you with recruitment.
Celebrating the impact of volunteers during Volunteers’ and Trustees’ Week.
Work with other CVS organisations and local initiatives such as Team Herts Volunteering supporting a culture of volunteering across Hertfordshire.
For any support that W3RT CVS can provide your organisation around volunteering, you can contact the CVS team by

or call 07908 209908.
